items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: The band was Sonny Wright on piano

ctx.x: and he said he used to ride as a kid. I told him I rode some and broke some ponies that my father had as a hobby for show purposes at county fairs, in Maine.

We had so much in common that we damn near self destructed. So on with the Ben Gazi incident. About the last of '47 or early '48, Ben asked me if I wanted to go to Washington, he was going to the Ben Gazi nightclub, it was a black club in the black district in Washington, D.C. The band was Sonny Wright on piano -- and oh, he was a lovely piano player, he made so many records that Teddy Wilson got credit for behind Billie Holiday, they sounded a great deal alike -- and Teddy Sturgis on bass.

And I took the saddle with me, as I discussed, and he checked us into the Dunbar Hotel, it was an all black clientele, and I was told at that time that it was the largest hotel in the world, up to that time. And I was the only white person to stay there -- there were hundreds of blacks. And Ben told the management and anyone concerned that I was to be looked out for, not to have anyone bother me, and he was looking out for my safety. And this was a reversal of the racial difficulties blacks suffered.
